Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Riya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lars: Good, thanks. Excited to see the hosted API demo.
[00:10] Priya: Hey, thanks. We mostly want to understand streaming and retry behavior - we have a customer-facing chat product.
[00:15] Jordan: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll cover - short demo of the API, show streaming, parameters, and then some retries and best practices. Riya will demo the console and a sample notebook.
[00:24] Riya: Hi all, quick note - when I say "streaming" I'm demoing both server-sent events and chunked transfer, depending on your client. We have a streaming SDK and a simple HTTP approach.
[00:34] Carlos: Quick Q - our current infra target is p50 latency 150ms and p95 under 400ms for one-turn prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?
[00:41] Riya: So typically p50 150ms depends a lot on model choice and sequence length. For our curated smaller chat models you can hit that but with tradeoffs in cost/quality. We can do burst routing and autoscale, but if you need strict SLOs Dedicated is better.
[00:55] Lars: We're more leaning hosted to start - faster time to value. Security wise we need SOC2 and SSO.
[01:02] Jordan: We are SOC2 compliant, and we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For stronger controls you can opt for the Private deployment later.
[01:12] Riya: Ok jumping into the demo - I'll share my screen, show the Console route for chat generation, then a notebook with streaming. Note: transcript may have typos, sorry if the auto-transcript butchered any names.
[01:25] [screen share starts, some background noise] Riya: Here is the Console, route creation, you pick a model from the catalog - we show latency/cost per 1k tokens, and recommend quantization or smaller variants under Optimize.
[01:40] Priya: Can you show the streaming example? We use websockets on web clients.
[01:44] Riya: Sure - example curl for streaming (SSE): curl -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat?stream=true" with an Authorization header. You'll get partial chunks with token deltas. In JS we'd use the SDK: client.chat.stream(...).
[01:58] Carlos: How do you handle retries? If a chunk fails do we re-request from start or resume?
[02:03] Riya: Good question. Streaming is best-effort; we recommend idempotency keys at the request level. For short interruptions, client should implement reconnection logic and request with the same idempotency key - our service will try to resume or you can replay safely. We also surface a last_token_index in some SDKs to help resume. (note: dev docs currently say last_seq in some places).
[02:28] Lars: Ok, so retry/backoff strategy?
[02:31] Riya: Exponential backoff with jitter; if you get a 5xx, backoff and retry with same idempotency key. For partial streaming failures we recommend a quick reconnect window (500ms-2s) then full replay for safety. Also use the session KV cache to keep context slim - it reduces latency and cost.
[02:50] Priya: Could you run an example with temperature and top_p? We tune for conservative answers in prod.
[02:55] Riya: Sure - in the chat payload: system and user messages, then params: temperature: 0.2, top_p: 0.9, max_tokens: 256, stop: ["\\n\\n"]. Lower temperature -> more deterministic. Also show presence_penalty/ frequency_penalty if you want to reduce hallucinations.
[03:14] [Riya types a request, partial streaming shown] Riya: You'll see token chunks come in - client receives incremental text and you can render progressively.
[03:23] Carlos: The client side is fine, but what's the overhead of streaming vs non-streaming for cost?
[03:27] Riya: Streaming doesn't change token billing; it's about UX and perceived latency. However more frequent commits to logging and telemetry can increase cost; Optimize suggests batching and prefix caching to reduce tokens.
[03:38] Jordan: On that note, our Optimize toolkit will run suggestions - batching config, cache TTLs, and recommend quantization profiles for your workload. We can share a short eval report after you run the trial.
[03:49] Lars: Do you support automatic fallback to smaller model to maintain latency during spikes?
[03:53] Riya: Yes - smart routing rules can fallback to compatible model variants. In hosted API you can set a route policy: primary model, fallback set, region preference, and cost tier.
[04:03] Priya: About data - retention, logs, can we turn off retention?
[04:06] Jordan: For hosted we offer configurable retention windows and option to opt-out of data retention for PII; for regulated workloads we recommend Private where you control logs and KMS keys. We have KMS integrations for encrypting at rest.
[04:18] Carlos: Is there an SLA for hosted?
[04:20] Jordan: Hosted has best-effort but we publish historical uptime; Dedicated has SLA and capacity reservations.
[04:27] Priya: Any known limitations on rate limits for streaming?
[04:30] Riya: There are per-account and per-route concurrent request limits; we recommend using our SDK with automatic client-side throttling to avoid bursts. We'll include limit guidance in the docs.
[04:40] [short silence, typing] Riya: I'll demo the notebook now - Node and Python examples. Here is code showing client.chat.create with streaming callback, handling partial events, and an example retry wrapper with exponential backoff and idempotency.
[04:56] Priya: The doc mentions 'continuous batching' - how does that work with chat?
[04:59] Riya: Continuous batching aggregates small requests for same model and hardware to improve throughput. For chat with low-latency needs we tune batch windows small (20-50ms) to keep latency low. Optimize will recommend window sizes based on your traffic shape.
[05:15] Lars: Competitors? We currently test against OpenAI and Anthropic. Curious how Redwood compares for cost/throughput.
[05:20] Jordan: We typically show 20-40% savings on per-token unit economics for many workloads due to caching and quantization; we'll share benchmark artifacts. Note: numbers depend on prompt shapes.
[05:31] Carlos: Any required changes to our auth flow to use SSO?
[05:34] Jordan: No, you can enable SAML and we support SCIM provisioning. We'll share the SSO guide.
[05:40] [two people speaking briefly, slight crosstalk]
[05:45] Priya: Ok next steps?
[05:47] Jordan: I'll send trial keys and a sample streaming notebook. Riya will attach the retry examples and Optimize quickstart. Please run a perf test with a representative prompt set, include sequence length distribution and desired SLOs. We'll follow up with a POC scoping call with infra (we'll include someone from our infra team to talk capacity and dedicated if needed).
